name: Bedford
intro: Bedford is a town in Westchester County. Its Recreation and Parks Department runs senior adult meetings and programs with free local rides for shopping and meetings, a senior advocate for residents and their families, and lunch and Meals on Wheels through an agreement with the Village of Mount Kisco.

seniorCenter.name: Town of Bedford Senior Adults (Recreation and Parks)
seniorCenter.notes: Senior adults meet regularly for talks, crafts, exercise, movies, parties and special programs. Call the Seniors Line to join the mailing list for the bimonthly calendar. The town's senior advocate helps all Bedford residents, including family members who live outside the town, with aging-related resources, caregiver support groups and help for people with movement or vision difficulties. A senior nutrition program and home-delivered Meals on Wheels are offered through an agreement with the Village of Mount Kisco.

transport.name: Town of Bedford senior bus
transport.notes: Free rides from Recreation and Parks for local shopping and senior meetings. Call the Seniors Line for the schedule. Bee-Line ParaTransit (914-995-7272) serves people who cannot ride regular buses, for a $5 fare.

more.name: Town of Bedford Senior Advocate
more.note: Free help for Bedford residents and their immediate family members, including those who live outside the town, with aging-related resources, caregiver support groups and grant information.

more.name: Town of Bedford Recreation and Parks office
more.note: 425 Cherry Street, Bedford Hills. Open Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.

sources: Town of Bedford: Senior Programs and Services
Westchester County DOT: ParaTransit Quick Reference

name: Blooming Grove
intro: Blooming Grove is a town in Orange County that includes the villages of Washingtonville and South Blooming Grove. The town's Senior and Nutrition Center serves a county lunch three days a week, and a town senior bus takes residents over 60 shopping in Monroe and Vails Gate.

seniorCenter.name: Blooming Grove Senior and Nutrition Center
seniorCenter.notes: Lunch is served at noon three days a week for people 60 and older, including Tuesdays and Fridays. Call ahead to reserve and to confirm the days. There is no fee, and a $3.50 contribution per meal is suggested. The weekly schedule includes a painting club, movie afternoons, mahjong, card games and bingo. Home delivered meals need a prescreening and an in-home assessment; call the county Office for the Aging at 845-615-3700.

transport.name: Blooming Grove Senior Bus
transport.notes: For town residents over 60, including Washingtonville and South Blooming Grove. The bus picks you up at home and goes to Monroe area stores and Woodbury Commons on Wednesdays and Fridays, and to Vails Gate and Newburgh shopping on Thursdays. A $1 donation is requested each way. Call Monday to Friday at least 24 hours ahead. Trips may be canceled if few people sign up.

library.name: Moffat Library of Washingtonville
library.notes: The library and its drive-thru window are open Monday to Thursday 10 am to 8 pm, Friday 10 am to 6 pm, Saturday 10 am to 5 pm and Sunday noon to 5 pm. The library has a home delivery service.

sources: Town of Blooming Grove: Senior / Nutrition Center
Orange County Office for the Aging: Senior Dining Program

name: Briarcliff Manor
intro: Briarcliff Manor is a village in Westchester County. The Town of Ossining's senior center extends home-delivered lunches and discount taxi coupons to Briarcliff seniors, and the public library sits in Law Park on Library Road.

transport.name: Ossining Senior Center taxi coupons
transport.notes: Discount taxi coupons for Ossining and Briarcliff seniors 60 and older cost $3 each, up to 15 a month, with proof of age and residency. They can be used in and around Ossining, Briarcliff, the Croton ShopRite and Phelps Hospital only. Bee-Line ParaTransit (914-995-7272) serves people who cannot ride regular buses.

library.name: Briarcliff Manor Public Library
library.notes: Housed in a 2008 addition to a historic train station in Law Park. Open Monday to Wednesday, Friday and Saturday 10 am to 5 pm, Thursday 10 am to 7 pm, and closed Sunday.

sources: Westchester County DOT: ParaTransit Quick Reference

more.name: Ossining Senior Center home-delivered meals
more.note: The center at 95 Broadway, Ossining, delivers a hot lunch Monday to Friday to qualifying homebound seniors in Ossining and Briarcliff, for a $3.50 suggested contribution. Call for program guidelines.

name: Bronxville
intro: Bronxville is a village in the Town of Eastchester. Older residents can use Eastchester Senior Programs and Services, including medical rides and the senior center at Lake Isle, and the Bronxville Senior Citizens club meets twice a week at the Reformed Church on Pondfield Road.

seniorCenter.name: Bronxville Senior Citizens
seniorCenter.address: The Reformed Church of Bronxville, 180 Pondfield Road, Bronxville, NY 10708
seniorCenter.notes: A club for people 55 and older, run by the nonprofit Senior Citizens Council with support from the Town of Eastchester. It meets Tuesdays and Thursdays, September through July, and is closed in August. Membership is open to all who consider Bronxville their community; dues are $175 a year ($87.50 for members 90 and older). Programs include exercise, chair yoga, tai chi, line dancing, bridge, mah-jongg, canasta and talks; luncheons and day trips cost extra. Bronxville residents 60 and older can also use the Town of Eastchester's Center at Lake Isle (660 White Plains Road, 914-337-0390), which serves lunch daily and offers rides to residents of Eastchester, Tuckahoe and Bronxville. The county lists the lunch site as temporarily at the Tuckahoe Community Center, 71 Columbus Avenue, so call to confirm where lunch is served.

transport.name: Eastchester Senior Programs medical rides
transport.notes: Rides to medical appointments for residents 60 and older of Eastchester, Tuckahoe and Bronxville, Monday to Friday, 9 am to 2 pm, by reservation. A free escort gives light help when needed. Suggested round trip contributions are voluntary, at $5 within Eastchester, Tuckahoe, Bronxville and Scarsdale Village, $8 to Scarsdale, Mount Vernon, New Rochelle and Yonkers, and $10 to White Plains, Hartsdale and Harrison. The town also offers shopping and errand rides. Bee-Line ParaTransit (914-995-7272) serves people who cannot ride regular buses.

library.name: Bronxville Public Library
library.notes: The library lists resources for people with low vision.

sources: Town of Eastchester: Senior Programs and Services
Town of Eastchester: Medical transportation flyer (Oct 2026)
Westchester County DSPS: Nutrition Programs and Site Directory
Westchester County DSPS: Senior Clubs and Centers (D-H)

name: Chester
intro: Chester is a town in Orange County that includes the Village of Chester and the hamlet of Sugar Loaf, with Town Hall at 1786 Kings Highway. The Town of Chester Senior Center is the hub for residents 60 and older, with exercise classes, games and a county senior lunch twice a week, and a Dial-A-Ride bus serves Chester and Goshen.

seniorCenter.name: Town of Chester Senior Center
seniorCenter.notes: For residents 60 and older. Weekly programs include gentle stretch and exercise, chair yoga, mat yoga, tai chi, quilting, mahjong and open cards and games. Fitness classes cost $10 a month for residents 60 and older, and tai chi is $20 a month. The Orange County Office for the Aging serves a Senior Dining lunch here on Tuesdays and Thursdays around 11:30 am for people 60 and older. There is no fee, a $3.50 contribution is suggested, and you must reserve 24 hours ahead at 845-469-7000 option 3 or by text at 845-325-7227.

transport.name: Goshen and Chester Dial-A-Ride
transport.notes: Curb-to-curb rides that must start in the Town of Goshen or the Town of Chester, to anywhere in those two towns. The bus runs Monday to Friday 8 am to 5 pm. The senior fare is $2. Call 8 am to noon on weekdays, at least 24 hours and up to a week ahead.

more.name: Town of Chester
more.note: Town Hall at 1786 Kings Highway is open Monday to Friday 8 am to 5 pm.

more.name: Orange County Office for the Aging
more.note: Aging Services Specialists answer questions about county services for older adults and can arrange home visits for homebound seniors. Bilingual help is available.

sources: Town of Chester Recreation: Senior Center (MyRec)
Town of Chester Recreation: Senior Center facility calendar
Orange County Office for the Aging: Senior Dining Program
Orange County Office for the Aging

name: Clarkstown
intro: Clarkstown is a town in Rockland County, with Town Hall at 10 Maple Avenue in New City. Its communities include New City, Nanuet, Congers, West Nyack and Bardonia. Older residents can join nine town senior clubs, ride the town Mini Trans bus at a reduced fare, and get lunch at the Meals on Wheels center in Nanuet.

seniorCenter.name: Clarkstown/Pearl River Senior Activity Center (Meals on Wheels Rockland)
seniorCenter.notes: Free to join for Rockland residents 60 and older. Open Monday to Friday, 10 am to 2 pm, and closed on holidays and bad weather days. Lunch is made daily, with kosher, therapeutic and mechanically altered choices. The suggested donation is $4 for lunch and $2 for a ride, and no one is refused service for not giving. Call or fill out the center's online form to join.

transport.name: Clarkstown Mini Trans
transport.notes: The town bus runs five routes that all meet at the Nanuet Mall. It runs Monday to Friday 6:55 am to 8:05 pm and Saturday 9 am to 7:10 pm, with no Sunday service. The senior and disabled fare is $0.40. It also gives weekday door-to-door rides to the Clarkstown senior clubs and rides from senior complexes to local supermarkets.

library.name: New City Library
library.address: 220 N. Main Street, New City, NY 10956
library.notes: One of several public libraries in the town. Nanuet and West Nyack have their own.

more.name: Clarkstown Senior Citizen Clubs
more.note: Nine town clubs for Clarkstown residents 55 and older meet weekly in Congers, Nanuet, New City and West Nyack. A free Senior ID card, good for five years, is needed to use town community centers, pools and the Stay Fit program. The phone is the town's main line.

more.name: Stay Fit Seniors (Clarkstown Parks and Recreation)
more.note: A 30-minute circuit wellness program for people 60 and older at the Street Community Center in New City. You must sign up ahead.

more.name: Town of Clarkstown Assessor
more.note: Call with questions about property tax exemptions for older homeowners.

more.name: TRIPS Paratransit (Rockland County)
more.note: County shared-ride bus for residents 60 and older who find the regular buses hard to use. For help applying, the county lists 845-364-2065.

places.name: Rockland Lake State Park
places.note: At 299 Rockland Lake Road in Valley Cottage. A 3.2-mile paved trail for walkers and cyclists circles the lake, and the park has picnic areas with tables. Open year round, daylight to dusk; a $10 vehicle fee is collected on spring and fall weekends and holidays and every day in summer.

name: Cornwall
intro: Cornwall is a town in Orange County, with Town Hall at 183 Main Street. Munger Cottage on Munger Drive is the town's senior center, and the county Office for the Aging serves a senior lunch there three days a week. The Cornwall Public Library on Hudson Street is an accessible building.

seniorCenter.name: Munger Cottage Senior Center
seniorCenter.notes: The Orange County Office for the Aging Senior Dining Program serves a noon lunch here on Monday, Thursday and Friday for people 60 and older. There is no fee, a $3.50 contribution is suggested, and you must reserve 24 hours ahead at the number listed. The town also uses Munger Cottage as a backup warming center, opened only when the Cornwall Office of Emergency Management activates it (845-534-8100).

library.name: Cornwall Public Library
library.notes: Open Monday to Thursday 9 am to 8 pm, Friday 9 am to 6 pm, Saturday 9 am to 4 pm and Sunday 1 to 4 pm. The library offers a homebound delivery service and is the town primary warming center during open hours.

more.name: Town of Cornwall
more.note: Town Hall at 183 Main Street is open 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, except holidays.

more.name: Orange County Office for the Aging
more.note: Aging Services Specialists answer questions about county services for older adults and can arrange home visits for homebound seniors. Bilingual help is available.

sources: Orange County Office for the Aging: Senior Dining Program

name: Cortlandt
intro: Cortlandt is a town in northwestern Westchester County, on the Hudson River, that includes the villages of Buchanan and Croton-on-Hudson. The town's senior services, called The Cortlandt Golden Connection, run from the Muriel H. Morabito Community Center in Cortlandt Manor for town residents 60 and older, with lunch, a weekday bus and senior clubs.

seniorCenter.name: Muriel H. Morabito Community Center (The Cortlandt Golden Connection)
seniorCenter.notes: Programs and services are for Town of Cortlandt residents 60 and older. The county lists the center for congregate lunch and home-delivered meals. The Cortlandt, Nor-Cort and Crompond senior clubs meet here. To reserve lunch, call 914-528-5164 the day before by 11 am.

transport.name: Cortlandt senior bus to the Community Center
transport.notes: Runs Monday to Friday to the Morabito Community Center for lunch and senior programs, with morning pickup and afternoon return. The contribution is $3 round trip, and the bus needs at least 6 riders to run. Call the day before by 11 am; some restrictions apply. For other trips, Bee-Line ParaTransit (914-995-7272) serves people who cannot ride regular buses.

sources: Town of Cortlandt: Bus Transportation to the Community Center

name: Crawford (Pine Bush)
intro: Crawford is a town in Orange County that includes the hamlet of Pine Bush. The Pine Bush Seniors club for people 55 and older meets every Tuesday at the Town of Crawford Community Center on Route 302, and the Town of Montgomery's Senior Bus and Dial-A-Bus also serve Crawford.

seniorCenter.name: Town of Crawford Community Center (Pine Bush Seniors)
seniorCenter.notes: The Pine Bush Seniors welcome everyone 55 and older. Meetings are on Tuesdays. Doors open at 11 am for social time, with a short business meeting at 12:15 pm. Your first three meetings are free, then dues are $2 a meeting, and members 90 and older pay nothing. Meetings include bingo, speakers and holiday luncheons, and the club runs bus trips. No meeting when Pine Bush schools are closed or have a two-hour weather delay.

transport.name: Town of Montgomery Senior Bus and Dial-A-Bus
transport.notes: Both buses run in the towns of Montgomery and Crawford, including Pine Bush, Thompson Ridge, Bullville and Searsville. The Senior Bus is free for people 60 and older (donations encouraged) and makes two medical runs a month to Middletown. Seniors can also ride the Dial-A-Bus for $0.50. Call 9 am to noon on weekdays, at least a day ahead.

sources: Town of Crawford: Pine Bush Seniors Club

name: Croton-on-Hudson
intro: Croton-on-Hudson is a village in the Town of Cortlandt. The village keeps a seniors contact at the Stanley H. Kellerhouse Municipal Building, and because most Croton residents also live in the Town of Cortlandt, they can use Cortlandt's senior lunch, home-delivered meals, rides and social worker at the Morabito Community Center.

seniorCenter.name: Village of Croton-on-Hudson Seniors (Stanley H. Kellerhouse Municipal Building)
seniorCenter.notes: The village's Seniors contact is at this building. Its resource page for adults 60 and older points to the Town of Cortlandt (classes, trips, meals at the Muriel H. Morabito Community Center and home-delivered, transportation and social worker consultations, 914-528-8377), Croton Caring (914-271-4979) for social programs, and the United Way 2-1-1 helpline.

transport.name: Cortlandt senior bus to the Community Center
transport.notes: For Town of Cortlandt residents 60 and older, which includes most Croton residents. Runs Monday to Friday to the Morabito Community Center for lunch and programs, $3 round trip, with at least 6 riders needed. Call the day before by 11 am. Bee-Line ParaTransit (914-995-7272) serves people who cannot ride regular buses.

library.name: Croton Free Library
library.notes: Open Monday 1 to 9 pm, Tuesday and Thursday 10 am to 9 pm, Wednesday and Friday 10 am to 5:30 pm, Saturday 10 am to 5 pm and Sunday 1 to 5 pm.

sources: Village of Croton-on-Hudson: Resources for Older Adults and Their Caregivers
Town of Cortlandt: Bus Transportation to the Community Center

name: Dobbs Ferry
intro: Dobbs Ferry is a village in the Town of Greenburgh. Its Senior Citizen Program serves residents 60 and older at the Embassy Center on Palisade Street, with classes, a weekday lunch, a village senior bus and referral help.

seniorCenter.name: Embassy Community Center (Dobbs Ferry Senior Citizen Program)
seniorCenter.notes: Activities include tai chi, yoga, exercise, arts and crafts, bingo, bridge, mah-jongg, movies, computer lessons, drama readings, trips and monthly holiday luncheons. Lunch is served weekdays starting at 11 am, for a $3 suggested contribution. Call before 11 am at least one day ahead; there are no walk-ins for lunch. Homebound seniors can have lunch delivered by calling the same number. The village also lists 914-231-8566 for the nutrition program.

transport.name: Dobbs Ferry senior citizen bus
transport.notes: The village senior bus runs every weekday. Call before 9:30 am on the day you need a ride. Bee-Line ParaTransit (914-995-7272) serves people who cannot ride regular buses, for a $5 fare.

library.name: Dobbs Ferry Public Library
library.notes: Open Sunday 1 to 5 pm, Monday and Wednesday 10 am to 8 pm, Tuesday and Thursday 10 am to 6 pm, and Friday and Saturday 10 am to 5 pm.

sources: Village of Dobbs Ferry: Senior Citizen Program
Village of Dobbs Ferry: Senior Citizen Nutrition Program

name: Eastchester
intro: Eastchester is a town in Westchester County that includes the villages of Bronxville and Tuckahoe. Eastchester Senior Programs and Services serves adults 60 and older with medical and shopping rides, case management, long term care planning, home-delivered meals, small home repairs, Medicare counseling, and senior centers at Lake Isle and Garth Road.

seniorCenter.name: The Center at Lake Isle (Eastchester Senior Programs and Services)
seniorCenter.notes: The town's main senior center, at Lake Isle Country Club, offers wellness and exercise programs, trips and live performances, and lunch is served daily. Rides are available to residents of Eastchester, Tuckahoe and Bronxville; call for reservations. The county's club listing says the lunch site is temporarily at the Tuckahoe Community Center, 71 Columbus Avenue, so call to confirm where lunch is served. A neighborhood center at 235 Garth Road, Scarsdale, is open Wednesday and Friday afternoons (914-771-3340). For senior programs or the town social worker, call 914-771-3340.

transport.name: Eastchester Senior Programs medical rides
transport.notes: Rides to medical appointments for residents 60 and older of Eastchester, Tuckahoe and Bronxville, Monday to Friday, 9 am to 2 pm, by reservation. A free escort gives light help when needed. Suggested round trip contributions are voluntary, at $5 within Eastchester, Tuckahoe, Bronxville and Scarsdale Village, $8 to Scarsdale, Mount Vernon, New Rochelle and Yonkers, and $10 to White Plains, Hartsdale and Harrison. The town also offers shopping and errand rides. Bee-Line ParaTransit (914-995-7272) serves people who cannot ride regular buses.

name: Florida
intro: Florida is a village in Orange County that lies in the Town of Warwick, with a small part in the Town of Goshen. Three senior clubs for people 55 and older meet at the Seward Senior Center on Cohen Circle, the Florida Public Library is also on Cohen Circle, and the Town of Warwick Dial-A-Ride serves the village at a half fare for seniors.

seniorCenter.name: Seward Senior Center
seniorCenter.notes: Three Town of Warwick senior clubs for people 55 and older meet here at 12:30 pm. Florida Seward Senior Citizens meets every other Tuesday, Golden Floridians every other Wednesday, and Flor-Wick Friends on the first and third Thursday. New members can attend a meeting to join.

transport.name: Town of Warwick Dial-A-Ride
transport.notes: Curb-to-curb rides Monday to Friday 8 am to 4:30 pm across the Town of Warwick, including the Village of Florida. Call 8 am to 2 pm on weekdays, at least 24 hours and up to a week ahead. The fare is $1 for riders 60 and older, disabled riders and Medicare card holders, exact change.

library.name: Florida Public Library
library.notes: Open Monday to Thursday 10 am to 8 pm, Friday and Saturday 10 am to 5 pm and Sunday noon to 5 pm (closed Sundays in July and August). The library is all on one floor, with an electric door on the south side and handicapped parking nearby.

sources: Town of Warwick: Dial-A-Ride / Local Transportation
Florida Public Library: Hours and Directions

name: Goshen
intro: Goshen is a town in Orange County, with Town Hall at 41 Webster Avenue. The Goshen Senior Center on Trotter Circle is open on weekdays for anyone 55 and older, and a Dial-A-Ride bus serves the towns of Goshen and Chester with a senior fare.

seniorCenter.name: Goshen Senior Center
seniorCenter.notes: Open Monday to Friday for senior programs, with planned activities at no or minimal cost for Goshen seniors 55 and older. A Senior Commission advises the town and village on the center and meets the third Wednesday of each month at 10:30 am at the center.

transport.name: Goshen and Chester Dial-A-Ride
transport.notes: Curb-to-curb rides that must start in the Town of Goshen or the Town of Chester, to anywhere in those two towns. The bus runs Monday to Friday 8 am to 5 pm. The senior fare is $2. Call 8 am to noon on weekdays, at least 24 hours and up to a week ahead. There are no standing appointments.

library.name: Goshen Public Library and Historical Society
library.notes: Open Monday to Thursday 9 am to 8 pm, Friday 10 am to 6 pm, Saturday 9 am to 5 pm and Sunday 1 to 5 pm. A local history room on the second floor helps with Goshen history and family research.

more.name: Orange County Office for the Aging
more.note: Aging Services Specialists answer questions about county services for older adults and can arrange home visits for homebound seniors. Bilingual help is available.

sources: Goshen Public Library and Historical Society
Orange County Office for the Aging
Goshen Public Library: Local History Room

name: Greenburgh
intro: Greenburgh is a town in Westchester County that includes the villages of Ardsley, Dobbs Ferry, Elmsford, Hastings-on-Hudson, Irvington and Tarrytown. Its Parks and Recreation Department runs the Gerard J. Byrne Center for seniors at Anthony F. Veteran Park, a weekday lunch program at three sites, home-delivered meals and senior transportation.

seniorCenter.name: Gerard J. Byrne Center at Anthony F. Veteran Park
seniorCenter.notes: An 8,000 square foot, fully accessible center with an exercise and dance room, resource center, lounge and activity rooms, open Monday to Friday, 9:30 am to 5 pm. Most classes cost $35, and day trips are offered. The town's lunch program for residents 60 and older runs Monday to Friday at the Embassy Community Center (60 Palisade Street, Dobbs Ferry), The Neighborhood House (43 Wildey Street, Tarrytown) and the Theodore D. Young Community Center (32 Manhattan Avenue, White Plains). The suggested contribution is $4, and no one is turned away. Call 914-989-1807 one business day ahead to reserve a meal.

transport.name: Greenburgh senior transportation
transport.notes: The town provides rides to its lunch sites when needed; call the nutrition program to arrange one. For other trips, Bee-Line ParaTransit (914-995-7272) serves people who cannot ride regular buses, for a $5 fare.

library.name: Greenburgh Public Library
library.notes: Open Monday to Wednesday 9:30 am to 8:30 pm, Thursday to Saturday 9:30 am to 5 pm and Sunday 1 to 5 pm. Several villages in the town have their own libraries.

more.name: Greenburgh Home Delivered Meals
more.note: A hot lunch delivered each weekday to residents 60 and older who are homebound by illness or disability or otherwise isolated. The suggested contribution is $4 a day.

more.name: Greenburgh Parks and Recreation registration office
more.note: Open Monday to Friday, 10 am to 4 pm, for program sign-ups.

sources: Town of Greenburgh: Assessor's Office (six incorporated villages)
Westchester County DSPS: Nutrition Programs and Site Directory

name: Greenwood Lake
intro: Greenwood Lake is a village in the Town of Warwick. The Greenwood Lake Senior Citizens group meets four days a week at the Greenwood Lake Community Center on Windermere Avenue, where the county also serves a Wednesday senior lunch, and the Town of Warwick Dial-A-Ride serves the village at a half fare for seniors.

seniorCenter.name: Greenwood Lake Senior Center (Greenwood Lake Community Center)
seniorCenter.notes: The Greenwood Lake Senior Citizens club for people 55 and older meets here Tuesday to Friday, 10:30 am to 2:30 pm. The Orange County Office for the Aging serves a Senior Dining lunch here on Wednesdays for people 60 and older; there is no fee, $3.50 is the suggested contribution, and you must reserve 24 hours ahead at this number.

transport.name: Town of Warwick Dial-A-Ride
transport.notes: Curb-to-curb rides Monday to Friday 8 am to 4:30 pm across the Town of Warwick, including Greenwood Lake. Call 8 am to 2 pm on weekdays, at least 24 hours and up to a week ahead. The fare is $1 for riders 60 and older, disabled riders and Medicare card holders, exact change. NJ Transit buses 196 and 197 also stop in the village on the way to New York City.

library.name: Greenwood Lake Public Library
library.notes: Open Monday and Friday 9 am to 5 pm, Tuesday to Thursday 9 am to 9 pm, Saturday 10 am to 4 pm and Sunday 11 am to 3 pm.

sources: Orange County Office for the Aging: Senior Dining Program
Town of Warwick: Dial-A-Ride / Local Transportation
Greenwood Lake Public Library: About the Library

name: Harrison
intro: Harrison is both a town and a village in Westchester County. Harrison Recreation sponsors two senior clubs, one downtown on Halstead Avenue and one in West Harrison on Underhill Avenue, plus a weekday drop-in center and monthly free blood pressure checks.

seniorCenter.name: Harrison Community Center (senior drop-in center)
seniorCenter.notes: The drop-in center is open Monday to Friday, 10 am to 4 pm, for TV, cards and socializing, with an exercise class Tuesdays from 10 to 11:30 am. The Downtown Group meets Fridays, noon to 3 pm, at the Veterans Memorial Building, 210 Halstead Avenue. The West Harrison Group meets Thursdays, noon to 3 pm, at the Leo Mintzer Community Center, 251 Underhill Avenue. Both clubs charge yearly dues and offer luncheons, day trips, movies and exercise and line dancing classes. A visiting nurse gives free blood pressure checks at both centers once a month, and county public health nurses give flu shots each October. Call for lunch, trip and ride details.

transport.name: Bee-Line ParaTransit (Westchester County)
transport.notes: County shared-ride, curb to curb service for people who cannot ride regular Bee-Line buses. It runs within 3/4 mile of a Bee-Line bus route, during the hours that route runs. The fare is $5 a trip, paid in exact cash or with a ticket, and a personal care attendant listed on the rider's ID card rides free. Book Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm, up to 7 days ahead; next-day trips must be booked by 5 pm. You must apply and be found eligible first (press 3 on the phone line for an application).

library.name: Harrison Public Library (Richard E. Halperin Memorial Library Building)
library.notes: The West Harrison Branch is at 2 Madison Street (914-948-2092).

sources: Westchester County DOT: ParaTransit Quick Reference

name: Hastings-on-Hudson
intro: Hastings-on-Hudson is a village in the Town of Greenburgh. Its Senior Outreach program at the James Harmon Community Center on Main Street gives free, private help to village residents 62 and older, from Medicare choices to housing and caregiver referrals, and posts monthly senior lunches and trips.

seniorCenter.name: Hastings-on-Hudson Senior Outreach (James Harmon Community Center)
seniorCenter.notes: Open Monday and Thursday 9 am to 3 pm and Tuesday 10 am to 3 pm, inside the Recreation Department office. Drop in or call for an appointment. Help includes telephone reassurance and home visits by appointment, Medicare plan selection, billing disputes, STAR and rent exemption questions, shopping and transportation referrals, home care referrals and caregiver support referrals.

transport.name: Bee-Line ParaTransit (Westchester County)
transport.notes: County shared-ride, curb to curb service for people who cannot ride regular Bee-Line buses. It runs within 3/4 mile of a Bee-Line bus route, during the hours that route runs. The fare is $5 a trip, paid in exact cash or with a ticket, and a personal care attendant listed on the rider's ID card rides free. Book Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm, up to 7 days ahead; next-day trips must be booked by 5 pm. You must apply and be found eligible first (press 3 on the phone line for an application).

more.name: Village of Hastings-on-Hudson (Village Hall)
more.note: The Senior Outreach worker can also be reached through the Village Hall line at ext. 644.

sources: Village of Hastings-on-Hudson: Senior Outreach FAQ
Westchester County DOT: ParaTransit Quick Reference

name: Haverstraw
intro: Haverstraw is a town on the Hudson River in Rockland County, with Town Hall at 1 Rosman Road in Garnerville. It includes the Village of Haverstraw and the Village of West Haverstraw. Older residents have a Meals on Wheels senior center with lunch on Hudson Avenue, a town senior citizens club that runs trips, and the county TRIPS bus.

seniorCenter.name: Haverstraw Senior Activity Center (Meals on Wheels Rockland)
seniorCenter.notes: Free to join for Rockland residents 60 and older. Open Monday to Friday, 10 am to 2 pm, and closed on holidays and bad weather days. Lunch is made daily, with kosher, therapeutic and mechanically altered choices. The suggested donation is $4 for lunch and $2 for a ride, and no one is refused service for not giving. Call or fill out the center's online form to join.

transport.name: TRIPS Paratransit (Rockland County)
transport.notes: A shared-ride bus for Rockland residents 60 and older, and for people with disabilities, who find the regular buses hard or impossible to use. Regular TRIPS runs 7 am to 7 pm Monday to Friday, with limited Saturday service from 8 am to 5 pm. For help with an application, the county lists 845-364-2065.

library.name: Haverstraw King's Daughters Public Library

Offerings include exercise, yoga, art, theater, crafts and music, an AARP Smart Driving course, tax-aide and e-filing, a computer lab with classes, and help with health insurance problems and Food Stamps (SNAP) applications. Seniors 55 and older pay $1 with proof of age, exact change only. Phones are answered Monday to Friday 8 am to 3:30 pm. Book at least three days ahead if you can, and no more than one week ahead. name: Newburgh (City)
intro: Newburgh is a city in Orange County, separate from the Town of Newburgh. Newburgh Area Transit buses run every 30 minutes on Broadway and reach St. Luke's and Cornwall hospitals and Vails Gate shopping for a $0.75 senior fare, and the Newburgh Free Library on Grand Street offers home delivery.

transport.name: Newburgh Area Transit (Transit Orange)
transport.notes: Wheelchair accessible local routes in the city that extend into the towns of Newburgh and New Windsor, with stops at St. Luke's Hospital, Cornwall Hospital, Mount Saint Mary College, the Newburgh Mall and Vails Gate stores. The senior fare is $0.75. No service on major federal holidays.

library.name: Newburgh Free Library
library.notes: Open September to June Monday to Thursday 9 am to 8 pm, Friday and Saturday 9 am to 5 pm and Sunday 1 to 5 pm, with shorter summer hours. The library offers homebound delivery for those who qualify, curbside pickup, and free computer classes and one-on-one tech help.

more.name: Transit Orange ADA Paratransit (Newburgh area)
more.note: Shared, wheelchair lift-equipped rides for people whose disability keeps them from using the bus, for trips within three quarters of a mile of a bus route. You must apply and be approved first; call 845-615-3850 for an application. The one-way fare is $0.75.

more.name: Orange County Office for the Aging
more.note: Aging Services Specialists answer questions about county services for older adults and can arrange home visits for homebound seniors. Bilingual help is available.

name: North Castle (Armonk)
intro: North Castle is a town in Westchester County made up of the hamlets of Armonk, Banksville and North White Plains. Its Parks and Recreation Department runs a senior drop-in center at the Hergenhan Recreation Center in Armonk four days a week, with door to door rides, weekly grocery trips and home-delivered meals.

seniorCenter.name: North Castle Senior Recreation (Hergenhan Recreation Center)
seniorCenter.notes: Seniors meet Mondays, Wednesdays, Thursdays and Fridays at the Hergenhan center in Armonk. Home-delivered meals are available to senior residents Monday to Friday, except holidays, for a per-meal fee billed monthly (914-273-3000 ext. 49).

transport.name: North Castle senior transportation
transport.notes: Door to door rides to the senior drop-in center four days a week, plus a weekly grocery trip to ShopRite or Stop and Shop. Bee-Line ParaTransit (914-995-7272) serves people who cannot ride regular buses, for a $5 fare.

library.name: North Castle Public Library (Armonk Branch)
library.notes: The North White Plains Branch is at 10 Clove Road (914-948-6359).

sources: Town of North Castle: Parks and Recreation FAQ
Westchester County DOT: ParaTransit Quick Reference

name: North Salem
intro: North Salem is a town in Westchester County. The North Salem Community Center in Croton Falls doubles as the senior center, the town runs a door to door senior van for residents 60 and older, and home-delivered meals come through a partnership with the Town of Somers.

seniorCenter.name: North Salem Community Center and Senior Center
seniorCenter.notes: Open to residents weekdays, 9 am to 4:30 pm, with a lounge, Wi-Fi, TV, games, puzzles, books, coffee and snacks, plus free fitness, craft and educational programs. The North Salem Senior Citizens Club, which is not run by the town, meets the second Tuesday of each month at the firehouse at 301 Titicus Road; members must be over 50 and pay $15 dues.

transport.name: North Salem Senior Van
transport.notes: A new town van gives door to door rides to residents 60 and older for local shopping and programs. Contact the Recreation Department to book. F.I.S.H. (Friends In Service Here), a volunteer group not run by the town, offers free non-emergency rides, mostly to medical visits, at 914-733-6188. Bee-Line ParaTransit (914-995-7272) serves people who cannot ride regular buses.

more.name: Somers-North Salem-Lewisboro Nutrition Program (home-delivered meals)
more.note: A hot weekday lunch delivered to residents 60 and older who need help for health reasons. Suggested donation $3 per meal.

sources: Town of North Salem: Senior Services
Town of North Salem: Senior Nutrition Programs
Westchester County DOT: ParaTransit Quick Reference

name: Nyack
intro: Nyack is a village in the Towns of Orangetown and Clarkstown, with Village Hall at 9 North Broadway. The Nyack Senior Activity Center on Depew Avenue serves a daily lunch, and the Nyack Library on South Broadway mails books to people who can't get to the library.

seniorCenter.name: Nyack Senior Activity Center (Meals on Wheels Rockland)
seniorCenter.notes: Free to join for Rockland residents 60 and older. Open Monday to Friday, 10 am to 2 pm, and closed on holidays and bad weather days. Lunch is made daily, with kosher, therapeutic and mechanically altered choices. The suggested donation is $4 for lunch and $2 for a ride, and no one is refused service for not giving. Call or fill out the center's online form to join. The village says the center offers exercise classes and computer workshops with the Nyack Library.

transport.name: TRIPS Paratransit (Rockland County)
transport.notes: A shared-ride bus for Rockland residents 60 and older, and for people with disabilities, who find the regular buses hard or impossible to use. Regular TRIPS runs 7 am to 7 pm Monday to Friday, with limited Saturday service from 8 am to 5 pm. For help with an application, the county lists 845-364-2065.

library.name: Nyack Library
library.notes: The free Homebound Delivery Service mails library materials to people who can't visit because of illness, disability or age. Call 845-358-3370, ext. 235 or 214.

more.name: Village of Nyack, Village Hall
more.note: 9 North Broadway, Nyack.

more.name: Orangetown Nyack senior club
more.note: An Orangetown senior club meets at St. Ann's cafeteria, 33 Jefferson Street, on the 2nd and 4th Wednesday at 2 pm. The phone is Orangetown Town Hall.

name: Orangetown
intro: Orangetown is a Rockland County town on the Hudson River, with Town Hall at 26 Orangeburg Road in Orangeburg. It takes in hamlets such as Pearl River, Tappan, Orangeburg, Blauvelt and Sparkill, plus the Village of Piermont and part of the Village of Nyack. Older residents can get lunch at the Meals on Wheels senior center in Tappan and join the town's senior citizen clubs.

seniorCenter.name: Orangetown Senior Activity Center (Meals on Wheels Rockland)
seniorCenter.address: Tappan Reformed Church, 35 Kings Highway, Tappan, NY 10983
seniorCenter.notes: Free to join for Rockland residents 60 and older. Open Monday to Friday, 10 am to 2 pm, and closed on holidays and bad weather days. Lunch is made daily, with kosher, therapeutic and mechanically altered choices. The suggested donation is $4 for lunch and $2 for a ride, and no one is refused service for not giving. Call or fill out the center's online form to join.

transport.name: TRIPS Paratransit (Rockland County)
transport.notes: A shared-ride bus for Rockland residents 60 and older, and for people with disabilities, who find the regular buses hard or impossible to use. Regular TRIPS runs 7 am to 7 pm Monday to Friday, with limited Saturday service from 8 am to 5 pm. For help with an application, the county lists 845-364-2065.

library.name: Orangeburg Library
library.notes: Pearl River, Tappan and Piermont also have public libraries.

more.name: Orangetown senior citizen clubs
more.note: The town lists seven clubs by area that meet in Orangeburg, Nyack, Pearl River, Piermont and Sparkill, most twice a month. See the club page for each meeting place and time. The phone is Town Hall.

more.name: Town of Orangetown Assessor
more.note: Call Town Hall and ask for the Assessor's Office with questions about property tax exemptions for older homeowners.

places.name: Tallman Mountain State Park
places.note: Open year round, dawn to dusk, on Route 9W in Sparkill, with a walking trail, a running track and picnic areas. An $8 vehicle fee is collected on weekends and holidays from Memorial Day weekend to Columbus Day.

name: Ossining
intro: Ossining is a town in Westchester County. The town's Senior Services department, at the Joseph G. Caputo Community Center on Broadway, is open to all Town of Ossining residents 60 and older, with a weekday lunch, home-delivered meals, a daily check-in call, a grocery bus and discount taxi coupons.

seniorCenter.name: Ossining Senior Center (Joseph G. Caputo Community Center)
seniorCenter.notes: Office hours are Monday to Friday, 8 am to 3 pm, and the center is handicapped accessible. Hot or cold lunch is served weekdays at noon for a $3 suggested contribution; call a day ahead. Hot lunches are delivered weekdays to qualifying homebound seniors in Ossining and Briarcliff ($3.50 suggested). The RUOK (Are You Okay?) program makes a check-in call every morning, 7 days a week. A social worker is at the center 8:30 am to 1:30 pm for information and referrals (914-762-7655). Weekly classes include Stay Strong and Fit, chair yoga and line dancing. The center closes when Ossining Public Schools close for weather.

transport.name: Ossining Senior Center grocery bus and taxi coupons
transport.notes: A bus goes to the Croton ShopRite every Wednesday at 12:30 pm for seniors who eat lunch at the center first, then drives them home; the fee is $2 and you must reserve. Discount taxi coupons for Ossining and Briarcliff residents 60 and older cost $3 each, up to 15 a month, with proof of age and residency. They can be used in and around the Town and Village of Ossining, Briarcliff, the Croton ShopRite and Phelps Hospital only. Bee-Line ParaTransit (914-995-7272) serves people who cannot ride regular buses.

library.name: Ossining Public Library
library.notes: Open Monday and Thursday 9 am to 9 pm, Tuesday and Friday 10 am to 6 pm, Wednesday 1 to 9 pm, Saturday 9 am to 5 pm and Sunday 1 to 5 pm.

more.name: Senior Citizen Exemption (RP-467) information
more.note: The Senior Services page links the Senior Citizen Exemption (RP-467) application and the town's sliding scale letter for homeowners 65 and older. Call the senior center with questions.

name: Peekskill
intro: Peekskill is a city in Westchester County. Its Senior Club and nutrition center at the Neighborhood Center on Nelson Avenue serve residents 60 and older with weekday lunch, activities and a city bus to the center and to scheduled shopping trips.

seniorCenter.name: Peekskill Senior Club and Nutrition Center (Neighborhood Center)
seniorCenter.address: 4 Nelson Avenue, lower level, Peekskill, NY 10566
seniorCenter.notes: The club is open Monday to Friday, 9 am to 3 pm, for Peekskill residents 60 and older, with social, recreational, instructional and civic programs plus information and referral. Hot lunch is made on site Monday to Friday. The dining room opens at 11 am and lunch is served at noon, and Grab and Go meals are offered too. The suggested contribution is $3 at the center and $3.50 for homebound seniors. Reserve at least one day ahead.

transport.name: Peekskill senior center bus
transport.notes: The city gives rides to and from the Senior Center for senior activities and lunch, plus scheduled shopping trips two days a week. Call one day ahead (meal reservations by 12 pm the day before). The suggested donation is $1 round trip, and riders must sign a transportation waiver before the first pickup. For trips elsewhere, Bee-Line ParaTransit (914-995-7272) serves people who cannot ride regular buses, for a $5 fare.

name: Pelham
intro: Pelham is a town in Westchester County. Town programs are open to residents 55 and older at the Daronco Town House on Fifth Avenue, including a weekly senior club, exercise and yoga classes, card games and a medical van.

seniorCenter.name: Daronco Town House (Town of Pelham senior programs)
seniorCenter.notes: For Town of Pelham residents 55 and older. The Senior Citizen Club meets Mondays, 1 to 4 pm, with bingo, meetings and special events, and collects small monthly dues. Senior exercise runs Tuesday and Thursday at 10 am, yoga for seniors Friday at 10 am, and cards (bridge, mah-jongg and more) Wednesday and Friday afternoons. The Resident Emergency Assistance List (R.E.A.L.), run with the Pelham and Pelham Manor police, lets older residents sign up for check-ins during storms and power outages.

transport.name: Town of Pelham medical van
transport.notes: Medical trips only, Monday to Thursday, with the first pickup at 9:15 am and the last at 3 pm. Book 24 hours ahead. Riders sit in the back and must get in and out without help. Service covers Pelham, New Rochelle, Larchmont, Eastchester, Bronxville, Mount Vernon, part of Scarsdale and the Ridge Hill area of Yonkers. Bee-Line ParaTransit (914-995-7272) serves people who need more help.

library.name: Town of Pelham Public Library
library.notes: Open Monday and Thursday 10 am to 8 pm, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday 10 am to 5 pm, and Saturday 10 am to 4 pm.

name: Port Chester
intro: Port Chester is a village in Westchester County. Its Senior Community Center on Grace Church Street is open to all Port Chester residents 60 and older, with no income rule or membership fee, and serves lunch at noon plus home-delivered meals.

seniorCenter.name: Port Chester Senior Community Center
seniorCenter.address: 222 Grace Church Street, Port Chester, NY 10573
seniorCenter.notes: Open Monday to Friday, 9 am to 4 pm; Saturday hours (normally 9 am to 3 pm) are temporarily suspended through December 2026, and Saturday meals are handed out as take-home meals on Fridays. Lunch is served at noon, with a suggested contribution of $2 for residents and $4 for nonresidents; no one is turned away. The center has a library, computer room and pool table, with Zumba, tai chi, bridge, mah-jongg, bingo, art classes, day trips and movies. Medically homebound village seniors may get home-delivered meals on weekdays ($2 suggested).

transport.name: Port Chester Senior Community Center transportation
transport.notes: The center provides rides for village residents. Call for details. Bee-Line ParaTransit (914-995-7272) serves people who cannot ride regular buses, for a $5 fare.

more.name: Village of Port Chester (Village Hall)
more.note: 222 Grace Church Street.

name: Port Jervis
intro: Port Jervis is a city in Orange County. The city runs a Dial-A-Ride bus with a 50 cent senior fare that also reaches a few miles into the Town of Deerpark, and the Port Jervis Free Library is on Pike Street.

transport.name: City of Port Jervis Dial-A-Ride
transport.notes: Rides within the city limits and up to 3 miles into the Town of Deerpark. The bus runs Monday to Friday 6 am to 3:30 pm. The senior fare is $0.50. Call 8 am to 1 pm on weekdays, by noon the business day before your ride (by Friday noon for a Monday ride).

library.name: Port Jervis Free Library
library.notes: Open Monday, Tuesday and Thursday 10 am to 9 pm, Wednesday and Friday 10 am to 6 pm and Saturday 10 am to 5 pm. Closed Sunday.

more.name: Orange County Office for the Aging
more.note: Aging Services Specialists answer questions about county services for older adults and can arrange home visits for homebound seniors. Bilingual help is available.

name: Pound Ridge
intro: Pound Ridge is a town in Westchester County. Its Neighbor to Neighbor program, run by volunteers with the town Recreation and Police departments, helps older and disabled residents with rides to doctors and food shopping, hot meals when someone cannot cook, a reassurance call program and a medical equipment loan closet.

seniorCenter.name: Neighbor to Neighbor (N2N), Town of Pound Ridge
seniorCenter.notes: A community volunteer program working with the Town Recreation Department and Police Department. Services include rides to doctors and to food shopping at The Market at Pound Ridge Square, volunteers who shop for you if you cannot get out, hot meals delivered when you are temporarily unable to cook, senior social events, the Call Reassurance program, File of Life and a medical equipment loan program. The program is reached through the town's Adults 62+ coordinator at the Town House.

transport.name: Neighbor to Neighbor rides
transport.notes: Volunteer rides to doctors and to food shopping. Call to arrange. Bee-Line ParaTransit (914-995-7272) serves people who cannot ride regular buses.

intro: Ramapo is a town in western Rockland County, with Town Hall at 237 Route 59 in Suffern. Its villages include Suffern, Sloatsburg, Hillburn, Montebello, Airmont, Wesley Hills and New Square, and it shares Spring Valley with Clarkstown. Ramapo seniors have a town drop-in center in Montebello and a Meals on Wheels lunch center on New Hempstead Road.

seniorCenter.name: Town of Ramapo Senior Citizens Center
seniorCenter.notes: A drop-in center run by Ramapo Parks and Recreation, open Monday to Friday for Ramapo senior residents. The weekly schedule includes chair fitness, pool tables and card and table games. Chair fitness sign-ups open the Friday before, and game tables are first come, first served. Call the center to reserve an activity.

name: Rye
intro: Rye is a city in Westchester County. Rye Recreation runs a Senior Adult Program for City of Rye residents 60 and older at the Damiano Recreation Center, with exercise classes, luncheons, speakers and trips.

seniorCenter.name: Rye Seniors (Rye Recreation Senior Adult Program)
seniorCenter.address: Damiano Recreation Center, 281 Midland Avenue, Rye, NY 10580
seniorCenter.notes: Open to all City of Rye residents 60 and older. Members gather for exercise, strength and balance classes, Zumba Gold, Pilates, painting, crafts, games, luncheons and movies, with monthly speakers and shopping, theater and lunch trips. Advance registration is required for all programs and events. Email ryeseniors@ryeny.gov.

transport.name: Bee-Line ParaTransit (Westchester County)
transport.notes: County shared-ride, curb to curb service for people who cannot ride regular Bee-Line buses. It runs within 3/4 mile of a Bee-Line bus route, during the hours that route runs. The fare is $5 a trip, paid in exact cash or with a ticket, and a personal care attendant listed on the rider's ID card rides free. Book Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm, up to 7 days ahead; next-day trips must be booked by 5 pm. You must apply and be found eligible first (press 3 on the phone line for an application).

library.name: Rye Free Reading Room
library.notes: Open Monday to Thursday 9:30 am to 8 pm, Friday 9:30 am to 5:30 pm, Saturday 10 am to 5 pm and Sunday noon to 5 pm.

more.name: Rye Recreation Department
more.note: Main office at 281 Midland Avenue.

sources: Westchester County DSPS: Senior Clubs and Centers (Q-S)

name: Scarsdale
intro: Scarsdale is both a town and a village in Westchester County. Residents 60 and older can join the Scarsdale Seniors Club for exercise classes, summer aqua aerobics and reduced rates on trips and programs, and village members can get taxi vouchers for nearby medical visits. A free daily check-in call runs with the Scarsdale Police Department.

seniorCenter.name: Scarsdale Seniors Club (Village of Scarsdale)
seniorCenter.notes: Open to Scarsdale residents 60 and older. The club offers exercise classes, aqua aerobics in summer, and special rates for tennis permits, trips and programs. Call the senior citizen coordinator or register online through the village. The village also runs a free daily phone check-in with the Scarsdale Police Department, called Are You OK (RUOK). If no one answers after three calls, police go to the home. Call the police non-emergency line to sign up.

transport.name: Scarsdale Seniors medical taxi vouchers
transport.notes: Scarsdale Seniors Club members who live in the village can get a taxi voucher for local medical and dental appointments, preferably between 10 am and 2 pm. Call at least one week ahead; the voucher covers one way of the trip. Bee-Line ParaTransit (914-995-7272) serves people who cannot ride regular buses, for a $5 fare.

more.name: Scarsdale Edgemont Family Counseling Service, Aging in Place program
more.note: A joint effort of the Village of Scarsdale and this nonprofit at 14 Harwood Court, Suite 409. It offers in-home counseling and assessment for homebound residents, home safety checks, information and referral to vetted providers, advocacy and help planning for the future.

more.name: Eastchester Garth Road Senior Center
more.note: A Town of Eastchester neighborhood center at 235 Garth Road with a Scarsdale address, open Wednesday and Friday afternoons for residents of that area.

name: Sleepy Hollow
intro: Sleepy Hollow is a village in Westchester County. Its Recreation Department runs senior programs at the James F. Galgano Senior Center, a free senior van, and low-cost hot lunches delivered to homebound village residents.

seniorCenter.name: James F. Galgano Senior Center (Sleepy Hollow Recreation)
seniorCenter.notes: Most senior activities take place here, including exercise classes, yoga, pickleball, ceramics and trips. Some activities need registration and a fee. A monthly calendar is posted on the village site.

transport.name: Sleepy Hollow Senior Van
transport.notes: Free rides for seniors to doctor's appointments and other local services, plus a grocery trip every Wednesday morning. Call the Recreation Department before 3 pm the day before you need a ride.

more.name: Sleepy Hollow Meals on Wheels
more.note: Hot lunch delivered Monday to Friday, between noon and 2 pm, to homebound village residents for $3 a day, paid weekly or monthly.

more.name: The Neighborhood House
more.note: At 43 Wildey Street, Tarrytown. Offers programs for seniors from Sleepy Hollow, Tarrytown and nearby, such as chair yoga, memoir writing, art workshops, movies and a bridge and card club. The Town of Greenburgh also serves a weekday lunch here for people 60 and older (914-330-3855).

sources: Village of Sleepy Hollow: Senior Clubs, Activities and Resources

name: Sloatsburg
intro: Sloatsburg is a small village in the Town of Ramapo, in the western part of Rockland County, with Village Hall at 96 Orange Turnpike. The Sloatsburg Public Library is on Liberty Rock Road, and village residents can use the Town of Ramapo senior center in Montebello.

seniorCenter.name: Town of Ramapo Senior Citizens Center
seniorCenter.notes: A drop-in center run by Ramapo Parks and Recreation, open Monday to Friday for Ramapo senior residents. The weekly schedule includes chair fitness, pool tables and card and table games. Chair fitness sign-ups open the Friday before, and game tables are first come, first served. Call the center to reserve an activity.

transport.name: TRIPS Paratransit (Rockland County)
transport.notes: A shared-ride bus for Rockland residents 60 and older, and for people with disabilities, who find the regular buses hard or impossible to use. Regular TRIPS runs 7 am to 7 pm Monday to Friday, with limited Saturday service from 8 am to 5 pm. For help with an application, the county lists 845-364-2065.

more.name: Village of Sloatsburg, Village Hall
more.note: 96 Orange Turnpike, Sloatsburg. Office hours are 8 am to 4 pm, Monday to Friday.

sources: Ramapo Parks and Recreation: Senior Citizens Center

name: Somers
intro: Somers is a town in Westchester County. Its Senior Services department, based at the Van Tassell House, runs a weekday lunch, home-delivered meals for Somers, Lewisboro and North Salem, and senior bus rides to medical visits and shopping.

seniorCenter.name: Somers Senior Services (Van Tassell House)
seniorCenter.notes: Office hours are Monday to Friday, 8 am to 3:30 pm. The department covers meals, social programs and rides, plus information for seniors and their families on health, housing and money. Lunch is served at Van Tassell House Monday to Friday at noon for people 60 and older, with a suggested $2 donation; call 914-232-0807 to reserve. The Somers-North Salem-Lewisboro Nutrition Program delivers a hot weekday lunch to residents 60 and older who need help for health reasons, for a suggested $3 donation; the first meal arrives the day after you sign up.
seniorCenter.address: Van Tassell House, 100 Primrose Street (Route 139), Katonah, NY 10536

transport.name: Somers senior bus
transport.notes: Round trip rides to medical appointments for seniors 60 and older on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays between 10 am and 2 pm, with a $10 voluntary contribution; call to check eligibility. Wheelchair accessible buses are available. Door to door shopping trips for adult residents who do not drive run Fridays (groceries) and Mondays (other shopping), with pickup after 10 am and a $2 voluntary round trip contribution.

name: Spring Valley
intro: Spring Valley is a village shared by the Towns of Ramapo and Clarkstown, with Village Hall at 200 North Main Street. The Finkelstein Memorial Library is on Chestnut Street, and Ramapo seniors can use the town drop-in center in Montebello.

seniorCenter.name: Town of Ramapo Senior Citizens Center
seniorCenter.notes: A drop-in center run by Ramapo Parks and Recreation, open Monday to Friday for Ramapo senior residents. The weekly schedule includes chair fitness, pool tables and card and table games. Chair fitness sign-ups open the Friday before, and game tables are first come, first served. Call the center to reserve an activity.

transport.name: TRIPS Paratransit (Rockland County)
transport.notes: A shared-ride bus for Rockland residents 60 and older, and for people with disabilities, who find the regular buses hard or impossible to use. Regular TRIPS runs 7 am to 7 pm Monday to Friday, with limited Saturday service from 8 am to 5 pm. For help with an application, the county lists 845-364-2065.

library.name: Finkelstein Memorial Library
library.notes: Call or check the library's site for current hours.

more.name: Village of Spring Valley, Village Hall
more.note: 200 North Main Street, Spring Valley. Ask for the Village Assessor with questions about property tax exemptions for older homeowners.

more.name: Ramapo Senior Activity Center (Meals on Wheels Rockland)
more.note: Weekday lunch center, 10 am to 2 pm, in Murchison Hall at New Hempstead Presbyterian Church, 484 New Hempstead Road, New City, for Rockland residents 60 and older. Suggested donation of $4 for lunch and $2 for a ride.

name: Stony Point
intro: Stony Point is a Rockland County town on the Hudson River, with Town Hall at 74 East Main Street. Two senior clubs for people 55 and older meet at the town's Patriot Hills Senior and Community Center, and the county TRIPS bus serves residents 60 and older. The town lists two libraries, Rose Memorial in Stony Point and the Tomkins Cove Public Library.

seniorCenter.name: Stony Point Senior Clubs 1 and 2
seniorCenter.address: Patriot Hills Senior and Community Center, 19 Clubhouse Lane, Stony Point
seniorCenter.notes: For people 55 and older. Each club meets once a week at noon, on Monday or Tuesday, and offers monthly trips and other activities. Call the town Recreation Department for details.

transport.name: TRIPS Paratransit (Rockland County)
transport.notes: A shared-ride bus for Rockland residents 60 and older, and for people with disabilities, who find the regular buses hard or impossible to use. Regular TRIPS runs 7 am to 7 pm Monday to Friday, with limited Saturday service from 8 am to 5 pm. For help with an application, the county lists 845-364-2065.

library.name: Rose Memorial Library

more.name: Tomkins Cove Public Library
more.note: 419 North Liberty Drive, Tomkins Cove, NY 10986.

more.name: Town of Stony Point Assessor
more.note: Call with questions about property tax exemptions for older homeowners, including Enhanced STAR.

places.name: Stony Point Battlefield State Historic Site
places.note: At 44 Battlefield Road, home of the Stony Point Lighthouse, built in 1826 and the oldest on the Hudson. From November to mid April the grounds are open Monday to Friday, 10 am to 4 pm, weather and staffing permitting, and the museum and restrooms are closed. Access to the battlefield is free. Call 845-786-2521 before you go.

seniorCenter.name: Town of Ramapo Senior Citizens Center
seniorCenter.notes: A drop-in center run by Ramapo Parks and Recreation, open Monday to Friday for Ramapo senior residents. Call the center to reserve an activity.

name: Tappan
intro: Tappan is a hamlet in the Town of Orangetown. The Meals on Wheels Orangetown Senior Activity Center meets at the Tappan Reformed Church on Kings Highway, and the Tappan Free Library is on Main Street.

seniorCenter.name: Orangetown Senior Activity Center (Meals on Wheels Rockland)
seniorCenter.address: Tappan Reformed Church, 35 Kings Highway, Tappan, NY 10983
seniorCenter.notes: Free to join for Rockland residents 60 and older. Open Monday to Friday, 10 am to 2 pm, and closed on holidays and bad weather days. Lunch is made daily, with kosher, therapeutic and mechanically altered choices. The suggested donation is $4 for lunch and $2 for a ride, and no one is refused service for not giving. Call or fill out the center's online form to join.

transport.name: TRIPS Paratransit (Rockland County)
transport.notes: A shared-ride bus for Rockland residents 60 and older, and for people with disabilities, who find the regular buses hard or impossible to use. Regular TRIPS runs 7 am to 7 pm Monday to Friday, with limited Saturday service from 8 am to 5 pm. For help with an application, the county lists 845-364-2065.

more.name: Orangetown Tappan senior club
more.note: Meets at the Sparkill Fire House, 520 Route 340, Sparkill, on the 1st and 3rd Tuesday at 1 pm. The phone is Orangetown Town Hall.

name: Tarrytown
intro: Tarrytown is a village in the Town of Greenburgh. Its Recreation Department runs the Tarrytown Senior Center with weekly exercise classes, bingo and computer classes, plus a free senior shuttle for village residents 60 and older. Greenburgh serves a weekday lunch at The Neighborhood House.

seniorCenter.name: Tarrytown Senior Center (Village Recreation Department)
seniorCenter.notes: Weekly programs include senior exercise classes on Monday, Wednesday and Friday mornings, nickel bingo on Mondays, a computer class on Wednesdays, senior meetings on the first and third Tuesday, a monthly game day and a monthly movie. The club also runs trips and an annual picnic and holiday party.

transport.name: Tarrytown Senior Shuttle Bus
transport.notes: Free for village residents 60 and older; you do not need to be a club member. Weekday rides to the Senior Center, The Neighborhood House or local stops in the village and nearby Sleepy Hollow, Irvington and Greenburgh, 9 am to noon, subject to availability. Wednesdays at noon the bus goes to the ShopRite in Elmsford. Book up to a week ahead and at least 24 hours ahead.

more.name: The Neighborhood House
more.note: At 43 Wildey Street, Tarrytown. Offers programs for seniors from Sleepy Hollow, Tarrytown and nearby, such as chair yoga, memoir writing, art workshops, movies and a bridge and card club. The Town of Greenburgh also serves a weekday lunch here for people 60 and older (914-330-3855).

sources: Village of Tarrytown: Senior Citizen Services
Village of Tarrytown: Senior programs FAQ

name: Town of Newburgh
intro: The Town of Newburgh is a separate municipality from the City of Newburgh. Its Recreation Department on Route 32 runs senior programs and a Senior Van, in partnership with the Orange County Office for the Aging, that takes town seniors to recreation programs and shopping.

seniorCenter.name: Town of Newburgh Recreation Center (senior programs)
seniorCenter.notes: The Recreation Department, open Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, runs senior programs here. You can register online or in person at the office. The town also runs the Alice Desmond Center at 6 Albany Post Road (845-565-1326).

transport.name: Town of Newburgh Senior Van
transport.notes: Curb-to-curb shared rides for Town of Newburgh seniors to recreation programs and shopping, run with the Orange County Office for the Aging. It runs on weekdays, with the last trips by 3 pm. Book at least 24 hours and up to 14 days ahead; no same-day rides. There is no service when the Newburgh Enlarged City School District closes or delays for weather. Drivers help with boarding but cannot carry packages. Call the Recreation Department for current hours and the suggested donation.

library.name: Newburgh Free Library
library.notes: The main library is in the City of Newburgh, open September to June Monday to Thursday 9 am to 8 pm, Friday and Saturday 9 am to 5 pm and Sunday 1 to 5 pm. The South Plank Road Branch (845-245-4750) is open Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday 9 am to 5 pm, Wednesday noon to 8 pm and Saturday 10 am to 2 pm. Homebound delivery is available to those who qualify.

sources: Town of Newburgh: Senior Van Rider Policy

name: Tuckahoe
intro: Tuckahoe is a village in the Town of Eastchester. Older residents can use Eastchester Senior Programs and Services, including medical rides and the senior center at Lake Isle, and the Tuckahoe Senior Citizens club meets twice a week at Fr. Fata Hall on Wallace Street.

seniorCenter.name: Tuckahoe Senior Citizens
seniorCenter.address: Fr. Fata Hall at Assumption Church, 125 Wallace Street, Tuckahoe, NY 10707
seniorCenter.notes: A club for people 55 and older, run by the nonprofit Senior Citizens Council; the Village of Tuckahoe's Senior Center page links to it. It meets Tuesdays and Thursdays, September through July, and is closed in August. Membership is open to residents of ZIP codes 10707, 10708 and 10709, and dues are $85 a year ($45 for members 90 and older). Programs include exercise, tai chi, line dancing, bingo, art classes and talks; luncheons and day trips cost extra. Tuckahoe residents 60 and older can also use the Town of Eastchester's Center at Lake Isle (660 White Plains Road, 914-337-0390), which serves lunch daily and offers rides to residents of Eastchester, Tuckahoe and Bronxville. The county lists the lunch site as temporarily at the Tuckahoe Community Center, 71 Columbus Avenue, so call to confirm where lunch is served.

transport.name: Eastchester Senior Programs medical rides
transport.notes: Rides to medical appointments for residents 60 and older of Eastchester, Tuckahoe and Bronxville, Monday to Friday, 9 am to 2 pm, by reservation. A free escort gives light help when needed. Suggested round trip contributions are voluntary, at $5 within Eastchester, Tuckahoe, Bronxville and Scarsdale Village, $8 to Scarsdale, Mount Vernon, New Rochelle and Yonkers, and $10 to White Plains, Hartsdale and Harrison. The town also offers shopping and errand rides. Bee-Line ParaTransit (914-995-7272) serves people who cannot ride regular buses.

name: Tuxedo
intro: Tuxedo is a town in Orange County. The town points older residents to the Tuxedo Silver Dollars, a social group for people 55 and over, and to the county Office for the Aging for home delivered meals, in-home care and benefits help. The Tuxedo Park Library is on Route 17.

library.name: Tuxedo Park Library
library.notes: Open Monday, Tuesday and Friday 9 am to 5:30 pm, Wednesday and Thursday 9 am to 9 pm and Saturday 10 am to 4 pm. Sunday hours, 11 am to 3 pm, run from Labor Day to June.

more.name: Tuxedo Silver Dollars
more.note: A social group for Tuxedo residents 55 and over, listed on the town's Seniors page.

more.name: Orange County Office for the Aging
more.note: The town lists the county office for help getting home delivered meals, in-home personal care, Medicaid and Medicare, plus legal services and tax preparation.

more.name: NYSOFA Senior Citizens' Hotline
more.note: State hotline listed by the town.

sources: Orange County Office for the Aging

name: Walden
intro: Walden is a village in the Town of Montgomery, with Village Hall at 1 Municipal Square. Older residents can ride the Town of Montgomery's free Senior Bus, get county home delivered meals, and use the Josephine-Louise Public Library.

transport.name: Town of Montgomery Senior Bus and Dial-A-Bus
transport.notes: Serves Walden along with the rest of the towns of Montgomery and Crawford. The Senior Bus is free for people 60 and older (donations encouraged), with monthly out-of-town trips and two medical runs a month to Middletown. Seniors can also ride the public Dial-A-Bus for $0.50. Call 9 am to noon on weekdays, at least a day ahead.

library.name: Josephine-Louise Public Library
library.notes: Open Monday to Thursday 10 am to 8 pm, Friday 10 am to 6 pm and Saturday 10 am to 2 pm; closed Sunday. Cards go to Village of Walden residents and Town of Montgomery residents with a Walden mailing address.

more.name: Montgomery Senior Center (county Senior Dining site)
more.note: The county senior lunch site at 36 Bridge Street in the Village of Montgomery, for people 60 and older. Reserve 24 hours ahead.

more.name: Village of Walden
more.note: Village Hall is open Monday to Thursday 7:30 am to 4:30 pm and Friday 8 am to noon. Parks and Recreation is ext. 1524.

more.name: Town of Montgomery Assessor
more.note: Call to see if you qualify for the senior (aged) and Enhanced STAR property tax exemptions.

sources: Orange County Office for the Aging: Senior Dining Program

name: Wallkill
intro: Wallkill is a town in Orange County next to the City of Middletown, with town offices at 99 Tower Drive. Local senior groups meet at the town Community Center on Wes Warren Drive, and the town Dial-A-Bus gives riders 60 and older a $1 fare anywhere in the town outside the city.

seniorCenter.name: Town of Wallkill Community Center (senior groups)
seniorCenter.notes: Local senior groups meet here regularly, along with a quilting club. The center is just off Route 211. Call the center Mondays, Tuesdays or Thursdays for details.

transport.name: Town of Wallkill Dial-A-Bus
transport.notes: Shared rides to and from places in the Town of Wallkill outside the City of Middletown. Buses run Monday to Friday 7:30 am to 5 pm and Saturday 8 am to 3:15 pm. The fare is $1 for riders 60 and older, disabled riders and Medicare card holders. Book by phone 8 am to 2 pm on weekdays, or online; booking several days ahead is advised, and Monday rides must be booked by 1 pm Friday. Tell the dispatcher if you need the wheelchair lift. No service on major holidays.

library.name: Middletown Thrall Library
library.notes: The public library in neighboring Middletown.

name: Warwick
intro: Warwick is a town in Orange County that takes in the villages of Warwick, Greenwood Lake and most of Florida, plus the hamlet of Pine Island. Senior clubs for people 55 and older meet across the town, two of them at the Warwick Senior Center behind Town Hall. The town Dial-A-Ride and village shuttle bus give a half fare to riders 60 and older.

seniorCenter.name: Warwick Senior Center (Town Hall complex)
seniorCenter.notes: The center sits behind Town Hall. Two town senior clubs for people 55 and older meet here. Warwick Valley Seniors meets every Wednesday at noon and Warwick Golden Senior Citizens meets every Thursday at 11:30 am. Other town clubs meet in Florida, Greenwood Lake and Pine Island. New members are welcome; attend a meeting to join.

transport.name: Town of Warwick Dial-A-Ride
transport.notes: Curb-to-curb rides Monday to Friday 8 am to 4:30 pm across the town, the villages of Florida and Greenwood Lake and the hamlet of Pine Island. Call 8 am to 2 pm on weekdays, at least 24 hours and up to one week ahead. The fare is $1 for riders 60 and older, disabled riders and Medicare card holders (proof needed), exact change. A village shuttle runs on a set route seven days a week with no reservation, and the bus also makes trips to Goshen, Monroe and Harriman, and Middletown shopping and medical centers on set days. The bus cannot use driveways or private roads, and drivers cannot help riders once they are off the bus.

library.name: Albert Wisner Public Library
library.notes: Open Monday to Thursday 9 am to 8 pm, Friday 9 am to 5 pm, Saturday 10 am to 5 pm and Sunday noon to 4 pm. For curbside pickup or homebound delivery, call and choose option 3. Homebound service, by mail or delivery, is open to cardholders who cannot get to the library.

more.name: NJ Transit buses 196 and 197
more.note: The town notes these buses run from Warwick to New York City, with stops in the town and the villages of Warwick and Greenwood Lake and a free Park and Ride lot on Route 17A.

sources: Town of Warwick: Dial-A-Ride / Local Transportation

name: Washingtonville
intro: Washingtonville is a village in the Town of Blooming Grove. Older residents use the town's Senior and Nutrition Center and its senior bus, which serves residents over 60 in the village, and the Moffat Library is on West Main Street with a drive-thru window and home delivery.

seniorCenter.name: Blooming Grove Senior and Nutrition Center
seniorCenter.notes: Lunch is served at noon three days a week for people 60 and older, including Tuesdays and Fridays. Call ahead to reserve and to confirm the days. There is no fee, and a $3.50 contribution per meal is suggested. Activities include a painting club, movies, mahjong, cards and bingo.

transport.name: Blooming Grove Senior Bus
transport.notes: Home pickup for town residents over 60, including Washingtonville. Wednesdays and Fridays go to Monroe area stores and Woodbury Commons, and Thursdays to Vails Gate and Newburgh shopping. A $1 donation is requested each way. Call at least 24 hours ahead, Monday to Friday.

library.name: Moffat Library of Washingtonville
library.notes: The library and its drive-thru window are open Monday to Thursday 10 am to 8 pm, Friday 10 am to 6 pm, Saturday 10 am to 5 pm and Sunday noon to 5 pm. The library has a home delivery service.

sources: Town of Blooming Grove: Senior / Nutrition Center

name: West Haverstraw
intro: West Haverstraw is a village in the Town of Haverstraw, with Village Hall at 130 Samsondale Avenue. The Haverstraw King's Daughters Public Library's main building is in Garnerville, and the Meals on Wheels Haverstraw Senior Activity Center serves a weekday lunch on Hudson Avenue in Haverstraw.

seniorCenter.name: Haverstraw Senior Activity Center (Meals on Wheels Rockland)
seniorCenter.notes: Free to join for Rockland residents 60 and older. Open Monday to Friday, 10 am to 2 pm, and closed on holidays and bad weather days. Lunch is made daily, with kosher, therapeutic and mechanically altered choices. The suggested donation is $4 for lunch and $2 for a ride, and no one is refused service for not giving. Call or fill out the center's online form to join.

transport.name: TRIPS Paratransit (Rockland County)
transport.notes: A shared-ride bus for Rockland residents 60 and older, and for people with disabilities, who find the regular buses hard or impossible to use. Regular TRIPS runs 7 am to 7 pm Monday to Friday, with limited Saturday service from 8 am to 5 pm. For help with an application, the county lists 845-364-2065.

library.name: Haverstraw King's Daughters Public Library
library.notes: This is the main library. The Village Branch is at 85 Main Street in Haverstraw, 845-429-3445.

more.name: Village of West Haverstraw, Village Hall
more.note: 130 Samsondale Avenue, West Haverstraw. Office hours are 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, Monday to Friday.

more.name: Town of Haverstraw Senior Citizens Club
more.note: The town posts its senior club trip lists each year, including 2026. The phone is Town Hall, and the club page lists tohseniors@gmail.com for questions.

name: West Nyack
intro: West Nyack is a hamlet in the Town of Clarkstown. Two Clarkstown senior clubs meet at St. Francis of Assisi on Parrot Road, the Meals on Wheels lunch center is close by in Nanuet, and the West Nyack Free Library is on Strawtown Road.

seniorCenter.name: Clarkstown senior clubs at St. Francis of Assisi
seniorCenter.notes: The West Nyack I club meets Mondays, 1 to 4 pm, and the Upper Nyack club Wednesdays, noon to 3 pm, for Clarkstown residents 55 and older. The phone is the town's main line.

transport.name: Clarkstown Mini Trans
transport.notes: The town bus runs five routes that all meet at the Nanuet Mall. It runs Monday to Friday 6:55 am to 8:05 pm and Saturday 9 am to 7:10 pm, with no Sunday service. The senior and disabled fare is $0.40. It also gives weekday door-to-door rides to the Clarkstown senior clubs and rides from senior complexes to local supermarkets.

library.name: West Nyack Free Library
library.notes: The library lists a homebound delivery service.

more.name: Clarkstown/Pearl River Senior Activity Center (Meals on Wheels Rockland)
more.note: Weekday lunch center at 121 West Nyack Road, Nanuet, for Rockland residents 60 and older.

name: White Plains
intro: White Plains is a city in Westchester County and the county seat. The city's Recreation and Parks Community Center on Mitchell Place runs programs for older adults, and the county lists it as a weekday lunch site for people 60 and older. Greenburgh's Theodore D. Young Community Center, with a White Plains address, serves lunch too.

seniorCenter.name: White Plains Community Center (Recreation and Parks)
seniorCenter.notes: The office is open Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm. The county lists the center as a congregate lunch site for people 60 and older; register before your first meal, and the suggested contribution is voluntary. Call the center for the current senior program schedule.

transport.name: Bee-Line ParaTransit (Westchester County)
transport.notes: County shared-ride, curb to curb service for people who cannot ride regular Bee-Line buses. It runs within 3/4 mile of a Bee-Line bus route, during the hours that route runs. The fare is $5 a trip, paid in exact cash or with a ticket, and a personal care attendant listed on the rider's ID card rides free. Book Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm, up to 7 days ahead; next-day trips must be booked by 5 pm. You must apply and be found eligible first (press 3 on the phone line for an application).

library.name: White Plains Public Library
library.notes: The library posted that it will have new hours of operation starting December 7, 2026, so check its website before you go. You can also text WPPL to 66746.

more.name: Westchester County Office for People with Disabilities
more.note: At 148 Martine Avenue in White Plains. Listed by the county for ParaTransit questions.
